runners_data.name: Onslow Gardens
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist who has struggled in sim-going (9 from 15 starts, 0 wins, 2 places), carried a visor today and dropping back from 10f; at OR 57 he is exposed at this level and has to travel a long way from the back.|
runners_data.comment: Onslow Gardens has experience over today's trip and going, and a third four starts back gives hope he can rediscover that form — yet winless in his last five starts, a return to that kind of consistency remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Mount Mogan
runners_data.note: Laura Mongan's nine-year-old veteran is remarkably well-tuned to Lingfield AW with 3 wins and 5 places from 14 sim-going starts; Georgia Dobie takes the mount and his form of 2-1-5-5-4 reads well enough to suggest he will chase Bajan Bandit prominently throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Mount Mogan is hard to fancy, though a win two starts back shows he retains ability; he has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh at least.

runners_data.name: Manton Road
runners_data.note: Strong 8f form on this surface (1-3-2-3) and a legitimate winning chance at OR 55, but his natural hold-up style means he has been pushed into a midfield mapping; Callum Hutchinson will need to manufacture a clean run from a position that isn't ideally suited to how this horse travels.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Manton Road faces a stiff ask at the weights carrying 130 lb from stall 10, yet he does arrive in reasonable nick — a winner last time out and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Whitesnake
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's four-year-old is a hold-up horse by inclination whose best form has come over shorter (7f-6f, mostly on this surface); stepping up to a mile after 37 days off, and with only 2/5 sim-going positives at shorter distances, the trip and redistribution into mid-pack both work against him.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Whitesnake faces a stiff ask from stall 11 carrying 130 lb, though consecutive third-place finishes at least suggest she's returned to some consistency after two poor efforts earlier in the sequence.

runners_data.name: Withoutfurtherado
runners_data.note: The form string of 975-05 tells a bleak story on its own, and his Standard-going record (2/15, 0W0P) is the poorest in the field; naturally a closer who is being mapped into midfield because the field's hold-up population outstrips available rear-ground positions, so he faces a compound disadvantage today.|
runners_data.comment: Withoutfurtherado has run over today's trip and returns on a lively 23-day break, with our rating of 62 suggesting he holds more ability than his official mark of 55 implies — the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must prove he can convert that promise.

runners_data.name: Ocean Force
runners_data.note: Gary and Josh Moore's five-year-old is 63 days fresh and has a thin sim-going portfolio (1/4 runs, 0W0P); his natural hold-up style is another that the field's congestion has squeezed into a midfield slot, limiting his ability to travel into the race as he would prefer.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and without a win to his name in recent form, Ocean Force nonetheless brings distance experience and a our rating of 62 that marks him out as a live threat from stall three, though the 63-day absence is the one concern to weigh.

runners_data.name: Nubough
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old who has run on this surface for virtually his entire career (15/15 sim-going runs), and his two wins and five places underline genuine AW competence; wearing a hood for the first time and fresh from 91 days off, but his prominent profile suits the race shape and he is not out of this.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a 91-day break, Nubough faces a stiff ask off 129 lb from stall 12, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a second four starts back hints at better somewhere within him.

runners_data.name: Warrnambool
runners_data.note: Nick Littmoden's four-year-old returns quickly (9 days) with headgear additions (visor) and a modest record of 0W1P from 10/15 sim-going runs; his hold-up style pushed into a mid-pack slot is a secondary concern relative to a form line that reads 8-6-5-4-0.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Warrnambool makes this hard work, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp nine-day turnaround carrying 129 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 60 and the sole genuine front-runner in the race, which is his primary tactical asset; his 12/15 sim-going record includes a second and six places and he has shown willingness to front-run at this course and distance — the STYLE_FIT tag notes he is mapped as prominent rather than pure leader, but in this field he will be first to stride.|
runners_data.comment: Bajan Bandit shaped with consistent promise last time out, finishing third, and was second two starts back, giving him back-to-back placed efforts from draw two carrying 135 lb; experience over today's trip and going suits, and he looks the one to beat despite being yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave's partner has an excellent sim-going record (13/15, 3W7P) and is consistent enough in form to be a serious each-way contender; his hold-up style is genuine but with only 7f to 7f history in his last five runs, stepping to a mile is a question that needs answering.|
runners_data.comment: Dandy Khan arrives here third last time out and, while winless in her last six starts, she has experience over today's trip and going and steps up fresh enough on 16 days' rest; carrying 134 lb from stall seven gives connections something to work with, though a breakthrough remains overdue.

runners_data.name: Muy Muy Loco
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's four-year-old is 155 days absent — the longest layoff in the field — having won over 10f on this surface; the headgear (hood) is notable and his sim-going figures (12/15, 2W5P) are strong, but the drop to 1m from preferred 10f trips and the fitness query after a long break dampen expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Muy Muy Loco landed a win three starts back but has finished fifth and sixth in his two most recent outings, and 155 days off the track is a significant absence to overcome; he has run over today's trip and going, yet 133 lb from stall one adds further pressure on a rating of 58.

runners_data.name: Francisco
runners_data.note: Alfie Redman takes the 7lb claim on this hold-up horse who won over 7f on AW most recently; a quick turnaround (7 days), headgear (tinted visor and tongue tie), and a step up to 1m all need to stack up — his natural style and the crowded hold-up portion of the field leave him reliant on things unfolding perfectly late.|
runners_data.comment: Francisco showed a win five starts back and a third six starts back but has since posted three modest efforts, and whilst he has run over today's trip and going before, seven days between runs and a stiff 132 lb could further test his ability to recapture that earlier form.

races.paceDynamic: Bajan Bandit is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 1m Lingfield AW handicap and, critically, faces no genuine rival likely to press him hard from the outset, meaning he can control tempo and dictate a measured, sustainable gallop through the race. Mount Mogan and Nubough will attempt to track him in prominent positions, but neither has the profile to seriously challenge for the lead, leaving Bajan Bandit free to bowl along at his own rhythm. The field contains a significant cluster of natural hold-up horses — Withoutfurtherado, Whitesnake, Ocean Force, Warrnambool and others — who are redistributed into midfield on the map precisely because there is insufficient genuine pace ahead of them to fulfil their natural role; those runners are unlikely to get a true rear-group stalking trip, meaning they will be racing out of character and their effectiveness is compromised. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit a length or two off the leader in a prominent position and travel into the race, because with one pace-setter setting an uncontested gallop, the race is likely to be won from on or near the pace rather than from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bajan Bandit Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Bajan Bandit meets minimal early pressure and dictates a gallop that suits his stamina, gradually increasing pressure from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Bajan Bandit ping-pongs off the front end at a true but controlled pace, keeping rivals in behind until well into the straight, where his staying power on this surface — evidenced by 12/15 sim-going runs and a second at this course and distance — becomes the weapon; the lack of a serious pursuer means his lead is always comfortable enough to protect.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Mogan or Nubough track Bajan Bandit throughout and produce a strong late burst to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Mount Mogan, a prolific winner on this surface (3W5P in 14/15 sim-going runs), is ideally placed to sit a length off Bajan Bandit and pounce; Nubough brings 15/15 sim-going experience and a 2/7f course win that underlines his suitability for this exact scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Split Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the field bunches, creating gaps for the better-positioned midfield horses to slice through in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Dandy Khan, with a strong sim-going record (13/15) and a consistent second-half profile at this sort of trip, is best placed to take advantage; Manton Road's form figures of 1-3-2-3 at 8f on similar ground mark him as a genuine each-way threat if he can secure an adequate position despite being a natural hold-up horse redistributed forward.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Arrive Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If a contested early gallop somehow develops or a suicidal pace causes the race to collapse late, opening the door for deep hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires runners like Muy Muy Loco, Withoutfurtherado or Ocean Force — all true hold-up types forced into mid-pack roles by the redistribution — to suddenly find the race unravelling in front of them in the final 2f; the low probability reflects that these horses are racing out of their natural style and the single-pacemaker scenario makes a true collapse of the lead unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Bajan Bandit holds an almost unopposed lead — if he is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable gallop unchallenged into the straight, he becomes very difficult to reel in and the race may be over sooner than his price suggests.

Mount Mogan's course-and-distance profile (14/15 sim-going, 3 wins) is the strongest in the field; watch whether Georgia Dobie sends him up to track Bajan Bandit from the outset, as if he secures that position the race is effectively reduced to two.

The redistribution cluster — Withoutfurtherado, Ocean Force, Whitesnake and Warrnambool — are all genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield; if the pace is slower than expected and they hit traffic in the straight, a wall of beaten horses could block any late challenges entirely.

Dandy Khan's step up to 1m is his key question: his last 5 runs have all been over 7f and while his sim-going record is strong, watch whether Pat Cosgrave settles him comfortably in the first half or whether he pulls early.

Nubough is 91 days fresh and sports a hood for the first time today — Kieran O'Neill will need to find a rhythm quickly from a prominent position; if the hood has the desired effect and he travels kindly, his surface experience makes him an interesting each-way watch.

races.name: Follow @attheraces On X Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gunfighter
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse with a win and two places at this course and distance on Standard; John Butler's yard is firing (T14: 7/26) but the pace map forces Pat Dobbs to ride closer to the pace than suits, weakening the closing chance.
runners_data.comment: Gunfighter won two starts back but has posted a seventh and ninth either side of that success, leaving his recent form looking inconsistent; he has run over today's distance and going before, returns after 20 days with a trainer firing at 27%, yet 136 lb is a sizeable burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Sant Alessio
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who relishes Standard Polytrack; returned 50 days off and Rhys Clutterbuck partnership new, but the key factor is that this horse must lead and will get that position in a two-way battle for the rail.
runners_data.comment: Sant Alessio has a win and a second in recent starts, but a run of fourth, seventh, and unplaced since makes him hard to fancy ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, and 50 days off the track adds to the query, though he has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: State Of Madness
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's prominent racer has three places from seven starts at 7f on Good going and ran just 14 days ago showing freshness; the step to Standard AW looks the only query but form figures suggest adaptability.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, State Of Madness nonetheless showed promise with a second two starts back, and the experience of today's trip and going conditions stands him in good stead; 134 lb from stall five is the query.

runners_data.name: Double Time
runners_data.note: Veteran front-runner aged eight with headgear (ht) and a sole Lingfield win on Standard; will push Sant Alessio hard from stall to 5f and the fitness question after 28 days is relevant — Tim Vaughan limited to 0/1 in the last fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Double Time has experience of today's distance and going, and a win in his last five starts offers some encouragement, but three unplaced efforts since that victory — most recently a seventh two starts back — underline a horse in search of his best form.

runners_data.name: Dontspoilasale
runners_data.note: Tom Queally's prominent racer ran six times consecutively without a win, all on Good or Standard at 5-7f; has place form on this surface and distance (4th, 7f, STA) and 14 days fresh, but the 13/15 Standard starts showing only 2 wins flags inconsistency at this level.
runners_data.comment: Dontspoilasale is rated highest in this field and has run over today's trip and going, arriving here on a quick 14-day turnaround in good shape from stall six; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with placings proving elusive throughout.

runners_data.name: Starlight Sami
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who won impressively over 7f on Good and has two places from three Standard starts; George Bass takes the ride and the 34-day break is a slight query but the profile fits a pace collapse better than a contested race.
runners_data.comment: Starlight Sami won three starts back and was third four starts back, giving him a solid recent profile to build on, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the worry is that back-to-back unplaced efforts since that win leave fitness and form under scrutiny after 34 days off.

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: John Butler's course specialist with three wins from thirteen starts over 7f Standard — arguably the standout course-and-distance record in the field; Charles Bishop is an experienced handler and the 7-day turnaround reflects confidence, not concern.

runners_data.name: Yachtsman
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has won over 6f on Good and placed over 7f on Standard; Jason Watson rides and the tongue-tie applied adds an unknown; held up naturally and the 34-day absence is mildly negative, but the progressive profile at this level is a positive.
runners_data.comment: Yachtsman won three starts back but has disappointed since, finishing ninth last time out after 34 days off; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating edges above his official mark, though the 131 lb burden is no help.

runners_data.name: Powder Monkey
runners_data.note: George Boughey's three-year-old returns from 89 days off, which is the longest break in the field and demands caution; placed twice at 7f on Standard and Good, and Pat Cosgrave is a strong booking, but the layoff is a clear fitness question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked well down our figures among today's rivals, Powder Monkey has been running into mid-division finishes of late, and 89 days between runs adds to the concern, though he has run over today's trip and going and stall two is a neutral factor.

runners_data.name: Paranjape
runners_data.note: Millie Wonnacott (5lb claim) rides this three-year-old prominent/hold-up type who won over 6f Standard and has placed twice at similar distances; the pacifier headgear may help settle but the 46-day break and step back to 7f from mixed form adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of thirteen, Paranjape does bring distance and going experience to the table, though 46 days off and 130 lb from stall 12 are questions connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Red Hat Eagle
runners_data.note: William Knight's veteran relies on headgear (tp) and seven consecutive placed or winning efforts over 7f-9f on Standard show consistency; Taylor Fisher rides and the 12-day turnaround is positive, but the hold-up style in a congested field brings traffic risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Red Hat Eagle nevertheless brings distance and going experience to the table and, rated 77 on our figures, shapes as a lively contender from stall 7 carrying 137 lb, freshened by a 12-day break.

runners_data.name: Bold Suitor
runners_data.note: Georgia Dobie's prominent ride for Craig Benton has an extraordinary record on this surface (15/15 starts on Standard) with three wins and nine places over 7f and 8f; the blinkers are familiar and the 12-day freshness reads well — the course record is the defining qualification.
runners_data.comment: Bold Suitor ranks 12 of 13 on our figures, and back-to-back finishes of fifth and seventh in his last two starts make him hard to fancy here despite a win three starts back; experience over today's trip and going and a return after just 12 days are modest positives.

runners_data.name: The Bitter Moose
runners_data.note: David Probert's visor-wearing hold-up horse has zero wins from three starts on Standard and poor Lingfield form; 59 days off after modest recent figures make this hard to recommend, and the true closing style is compromised by a crowded rear in this field.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts at this level make The Bitter Moose a genuine threat, third in two of his last three starts and carrying experience over today's trip and going; the main risk is a 59-day absence that could blunt his edge.

runners_data.name: Dancing Rinca
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse placed in midfield due to the volume of closers in this field; Hayley Turner's seven-year-old (T14: 0/8) has struggled on Good recently and the pacifier headgear is new — Kieran O'Neill needs a clear lane that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Dancing Rinca makes the case hard to press despite drawing stall one and returning after a reasonable 20-day break; experience over today's trip offers little consolation given the limited recent form.

races.paceDynamic: Sant Alessio and Double Time are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely competitive early tempo over Lingfield's 7f Polytrack on a Standard surface. With six of fourteen runners wanting prominent positions, the middle part of the race between the 3f and 2f poles will be congested and scrappy, with riders fighting for rail room and clean air. The contested pace and honest gallop on a flat, fair track should set up a strong-staying prominent type or a horse that can sit just off the frenzied early battle and pick up the pieces — this race shape strongly favours PROMINENT runners who can track the pace at a sustainable clip and pounce from 2f out, rather than true closers who will be caught in traffic. The field holds more hold-up types than can operate cleanly at the rear: Gunfighter and Dancing Rinca are genuine closers but are mapped to midfield due to the rear being overcrowded, meaning Sant Alessio and Double Time are most likely to actually secure the front positions, with Split Elevens, State Of Madness and Bold Suitor best placed to hunt them down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sant Alessio and Double Time push each other honestly through the early stages and a prominent tracker hits the front 2f out.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners soften each other up through a brisk pace, leaving the race open for a horse sitting just behind in third or fourth — Split Elevens, State Of Madness or Bold Suitor are ideally profiled to sweep past the tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners gains a decisive lead through the first half and the field never collectively reels them back in.
scenarios.body: Sant Alessio's class edge at this level and proven Standard going form makes them the more likely beneficiary if the gallop flattens out through the middle furlong, with the pack too busy fighting each other to close; Double Time represents the same profile on a day when they get a soft lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns fiercely enough through the first 4f that even prominent horses are spent and a well-positioned midfield runner delivers the strongest finish.
scenarios.body: Powder Monkey or Paranjape, both tracking mid-division, would benefit from a collapse in the leading bunch if genuine attrition hits; Yachtsman is bred for this scenario having won at 6f on Good and may handle the step up in distance under a patient Jason Watson.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is extreme enough to leave the entire field strung out and a hold-up horse gets a clear run from 2f out.
scenarios.body: This depends on Gunfighter or The Bitter Moose finding a clean passage, which is made harder by their redistribution to midfield in an already congested race — their natural closing style is compromised from the start, reducing this scenario's probability sharply; Red Hat Eagle has strong 7f Standard form but is headgear-dependent and inconsistent.

watchPoints.text: Split Elevens (Charles Bishop) is the best-qualified horse on course-and-distance form with three 7f Standard wins — watch for Bishop to get an early prominent position and control the race from behind the front two.

Bold Suitor's 15-from-15 record on Standard going is unprecedented in this field — Georgia Dobie must place the horse in a prominent berth early to exploit that surface affinity before the field bunches 2f out.

The Sant Alessio vs Double Time duel for the lead in the first 2f is the key pace trigger — if Double Time pushes harder than expected and drags the tempo very high, even prominent horses like State Of Madness will be under pressure from the 3f pole.

Powder Monkey returns from 89 days off — watch the paddock for signs of fitness and monitor betting movement; if Pat Cosgrave positions handily from stall early, the layoff concern diminishes sharply.

Gunfighter and Dancing Rinca are both true closers forced closer to the pace than ideal — if either is switched wide at the 3f pole seeking daylight, that is a sign the rider is improvising and the chance may have already passed.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dark Mandate
runners_data.note: 302 days off the track is an enormous concern for a 3-year-old hold-up horse from Eve Johnson Houghton's yard, and similar-going form reads 2 from 7 with no wins; the long absence makes it very hard to trust at any price in a strongly-run race where timing of the run is everything.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 302 days, Dark Mandate faces obvious questions, but he has run over today's distance and going before and a third last time out shows residual ability; drawn at stall one carrying 132 lb, he merits respect on his overall profile.

runners_data.name: Solar Phoenix
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's 3-year-old is on just 13 days' rest and showed reasonable recent form but has no Standard AW wins from 5 attempts on similar going; a genuine hold-up type by style, though the volume of closers in this field means it may be forced to race more prominently than suits.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Solar Phoenix is hard to fancy at the weights, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and 13 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Pennine Way
runners_data.note: One of the three confirmed pace-makers and George Bass takes the ride for Jack Channon, who is 1 from 15 in the last 14 days; Pennine Way's best finish on Standard AW was a second over 7f, and dropping to 6f while fighting rivals for the lead may see it empty before the line.
runners_data.comment: Pennine Way has run over today's trip and going, and her recent placings — third one start back and runner-up last time out — show she is building nicely, though she remains winless in her last five starts and a rating of 57 suggests she faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Mister Moet
runners_data.note: Kieran O'Neill partners the most course-effective front-runner in the field — 2 wins and 5 places from 15 Standard AW runs is a standout record — and Scott Dixon is 2 from 21 recently; the key question is whether it can break away clean before Pennine Way and King Cherry crowd it out.
runners_data.comment: Mister Moet returns in fair order on a 15-day turnaround, and his second three starts back gives him a creditable recent highlight; however, back-to-back fourths in his most recent outings suggest he finds a way to get into it without quite asserting, and 131 lb is no help from stall 10.

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams has been in form with 5 wins from 33 runners over 14 days, and Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claimer) adds an allowance, but King Cherry's form string of 75867 offers no confidence it can front-run competitively, finishing 7th and 8th in its last two tries on Standard and Good.
runners_data.comment: King Cherry has run over today's trip and going, rates 7 lb above his official mark on our figures, and 15 days since his last start leaves him fresh enough to improve; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts and consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 3-year-old won over 6f Good and placed twice over the same trip, so the distance and form profile are genuine; its true style is hold-up, but with so many closers in this field it is likely to be jostled into a more prominent position, and the trainer's 14-day record of 0 from 22 is a significant negative angle.
runners_data.comment: Rated a pound below the official mark and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Lieutenant Sir faces a stiff ask, and a trainer without a winner in 22 attempts over the past fortnight does little to inspire confidence; he does return after 36 days with distance and going experience and a win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Fuseboard
runners_data.note: Chelsea Banham's yard is 1 from 3 in the past fortnight, and Fuseboard is the one horse in the hold-up cluster that has actually won on Standard AW (5f, last time out); a genuine closer by inclination, it will likely be unable to get its preferred position in this traffic-heavy shape, which tempers confidence despite the solid recent form.
runners_data.comment: Fuseboard has been largely out of the sorts in recent starts, though he did land a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before; ranked last on our figures and drawn 11 carrying 131 lb, he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Apex Star
runners_data.note: Taylor Fisher partners for William Knight (0/13 T14), and Apex Star's sim-going form of 5 from 9 with 2 places confirms it handles Standard AW; as a genuine prominent type that does not need to lead, it is ideally positioned to exploit the pace battle unfolding in front of it.
runners_data.comment: Apex Star has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, finishing third three times and second in his last six, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions — our rating of 65 suggests he holds strong claims here, though he remains yet to win.

runners_data.name: Reality Queen
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3-year-old is the highest OR in the field at 60 and has recent Fibresand win form, but Standard AW record from similar going reads 0 from 11 with no wins or places — a meaningful stamina concern for a hold-up horse in a strongly-run 6f handicap.
runners_data.comment: Reality Queen won one start back but has finished fourth on her most recent outing, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, a mark of 60 and draw three from 134 lb make her a solid mid-division type rather than a standout prospect here.

runners_data.name: Royal County Glory
runners_data.note: Jack Jones has 2 from 13 over the past fortnight, and Royal County Glory's Standard AW profile is the best in the field for a prominent type — 1 win, 4 places from 11 similar-going runs — with Jason Watson's course craft key; 80 days off the track is worth monitoring but the record here is hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Royal County Glory won three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, while his rating of 66 heads the field on the figures; the concern is a return from 80 days off and a run of ninth last time out suggest he needs to find his best.

runners_data.name: Mayfair Market
runners_data.note: Millie Wonnacott's 5lb claim helps, but S Woods' string is 2 from 8 recently and Mayfair Market has gone 7th, 9th, 8th, 6th in its last four — progressive decline in form; the hold-up style over a trip seemingly on the short side makes it hard to construct a winning scenario without a significant step forward.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mayfair Market has nonetheless run over today's trip and going before, and a 23-day break may have freshened her; she carries 133 lb from stall eight, and a rating of 63 gives her a slender edge to exploit if the form finally clicks.

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: David Probert is a strong booking for John Butler (7/26 T14 — the most active strike rate in the race) and Love Alive has a win from 13 similar-going starts; a true hold-up type, it needs the pace to collapse in the final furlong, which is plausible given the three-way lead battle but not guaranteed.

races.paceDynamic: Pennine Way, Mister Moet, and King Cherry are all confirmed front-runners in a 12-runner 6f Lingfield AW handicap, and with three horses genuinely wanting to lead, the early gallop will be strong from the outset — Mister Moet has the widest barrier coverage while Pennine Way and King Cherry will contest the rail aggressively, meaning no horse gets a soft lead and the pace is unlikely to relent. The middle portion of the race will be run at a sustained clip, compressing the finishing positions and stretching stamina reserves for any horse that has expended energy jostling for position. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently with tactical speed but not needing to actually lead — specifically Apex Star and Royal County Glory, both genuine prominent types who can sit just off the fierce early battle and pounce at the two-furlong pole when the pace battle takes its toll on the leaders. The field also holds more true hold-up types than the rear of the field can accommodate: Solar Phoenix, Lieutenant Sir, and Fuseboard are genuine closers who are likely to be pushed forward out of their natural role, meaning the runners most likely to actually secure their preferred position are Pennine Way and Mister Moet among the leaders, with King Cherry's modest recent form making him the most vulnerable of the three to being crowded out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Pennine Way, Mister Moet, and King Cherry fight it out from the front, setting a scorching pace that destroys their own finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: The lead trio will hit the home straight spent, handing the race to prominent-tracking types who have conserved energy behind the battle; Apex Star and Royal County Glory are ideally suited, having shown they can race just off honest gallops and finish strongly over this course and distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Moet breaks cleanest, secures a clear lead uncontested in the first furlong, and the other front-runners drop off the pace.
scenarios.body: Mister Moet has 2 wins and 5 places on Standard AW going from 15 runs and is demonstrably most comfortable on this surface — if granted even a half-length cushion, his tactical speed and course aptitude allow him to dictate a controlled pace and resist the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns so hot that the race completely falls apart at the front and hold-up horses get an unimpeded run through.
scenarios.body: Love Alive and Reality Queen are the truest hold-up types with legitimate closing form, and a genuine meltdown pace over 6f on Standard AW could just see them pick up the pieces; however, this scenario is discounted because Solar Phoenix, Lieutenant Sir, and Fuseboard — the other supposed closers — are likely to be racing out of role further forward than ideal, crowding the finish rather than timing their runs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the early chaos causes interference or wide runs that disrupt multiple horses, with the race effectively won in the first two furlongs by whichever prominent runner avoids trouble.
scenarios.body: Royal County Glory's course form (won at 7f Standard, placed repeatedly) and Jason Watson's positioning instincts give him the edge in a messy scenario; Apex Star's consistency in Standard going also suits a race where pure positioning rather than finishing kick determines the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Pennine Way, Mister Moet, and King Cherry will all contest the early lead aggressively — watch for crowding or checking in the first two furlongs that could compromise multiple runners behind them.

Fuseboard, Lieutenant Sir, and Solar Phoenix are true hold-up horses likely to be pushed forward out of role by the traffic — if any of them get caught wide and expend energy early, their chances will be significantly undermined.

Royal County Glory returns from 80 days off — watch the pre-race market and paddock closely, as a prominent type with that level of course form coming back from a break needs to show freshness rather than rustiness.

Love Alive is trained by John Butler who is among the most in-form trainers in this field at 7/26 over 14 days — if the pace truly burns hot and a late closer is to emerge, this is the one with the most credible handler backing.

Dark Mandate's 302-day absence makes it an almost impossible proposition to trust for competitive betting, but if it shows inexplicably sharp early speed it could become a factor in disrupting the established pace hierarchy — monitor its market drifts.

races.name: Download The At The Races App Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Queen Sana
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with five placed efforts from six recent starts, Jason Watson takes the ride for in-form Ollie Sangster; handles fast and good ground well but her OR-69 mark means she has to find improvement to get off the placed list.|
runners_data.comment: Queen Sana brings solid placed form to this, with a second two starts back and another runner-up finish four starts back among several close efforts, and our rating of 75 tops the field; the concern is she remains yet to win in recent starts despite repeated chances.

runners_data.name: Fiorella Princess
runners_data.note: Returns from a 134-day absence for Robert Cowell, whose 2/9 T14 strike rate suggests runners are coming in fit; her AW Standard record of 5 places from 15 runs is solid and she wears headgear — fitness after a long break is the only real reservation.|
runners_data.comment: Fiorella Princess has shown consistent placing ability, finishing second and third in recent starts, and has run over today's trip and going before, making her a genuine threat at a rating of 72; the main concern is 134 days off the track, leaving fitness the key question.

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner who has won twice on Good and once at 6f, but AW Standard form is thin (1 run, 13th); Elle-May Croot (5lb claim) handles pace-making rides and an uncontested lead suits her profile perfectly, making her the race-shaper regardless of finishing position.|
runners_data.comment: Sea Her Excel won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but a speed rating of 59 and a fifth two starts back temper expectations, and she faces six rivals carrying 134 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: La Belle Forest
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's filly has course-and-distance form including a win at Lingfield on Standard, but her natural hold-up style means she is squeezed into a midfield slot by the volume of rear-runners in this field — she is racing out of role and her chance depends on gaps appearing that may not materialise at 5f.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, La Belle Forest is hard to fancy, especially with the trainer yet to strike from 22 attempts in the last fortnight; she has run over today's trip and going before, and stall three is hers from 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Whizzy Dizzy
runners_data.note: Clive Cox has been busy (6/22 T14) and this filly's AW 5f form shows consistent mid-division finishes; Georgia Dobie takes the ride, and as a genuine hold-up type she needs the pace to be genuinely strong to deliver her effort in time over the minimum trip.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of mid-to-rear finishes capped by a seventh last time out, Whizzy Dizzy ranks last on our figures and is hard to fancy despite the in-form yard and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Little Jaybee
runners_data.note: David Evans pitches her back up quickly after just 8 days, which can suit his yard; a true hold-up runner placed into midfield on the map because of the congested rear, her STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 tempers confidence — Pat Cosgrave's experience is an asset but she needs things to go her way.|

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's 4-year-old has been relentlessly consistent, running into a place in five of her last six starts on Good ground at 5f; David Probert takes over and her prominent style maps perfectly to the expected race shape — notable that all recent form is on Good, and Standard AW is an unknown surface switch.|
runners_data.comment: Placed in four of her last six starts, Over Spiced arrives on a sharp 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour; the chief concern is that she remains yet to win despite her recent string of near-misses.

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Jim & Suzi Best who usually contests longer trips (6-8f) and is stepping back to the minimum; a hold-up operator on Good ground who hasn't run on AW Standard recently, and Tom Queally faces a challenge getting him competitive in a race not set up for closers.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last six starts, Independent Expert nonetheless brings strong fitness credentials having run just 17 days ago, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — her fourth last time out represents her best recent effort, and a rating of 75 makes her a lively alternative to the top-rated runner.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Her Excel is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from gate to line over Lingfield's straight 5f on a Standard AW surface. Queen Sana, Fiorella Princess, and Over Spiced will push for prominent positions just behind, creating a competitive but not chaotic early order that keeps pressure on the leader without turning it into a sprint for supremacy. The field does contain more hold-up intent than can be accommodated at the rear — La Belle Forest and Little Jaybee are true hold-up horses pushed into the midfield mapping because Whizzy Dizzy and Independent Expert already occupy the genuine backmarker slots, meaning those two redistributed runners are unlikely to get the late space their style demands. With one unchallenged pace-setter and a clutch of prominent types close behind, this race shape most favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort through the final furlong rather than those relying on a late closing run that the honest but unhurried gallop may never set up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sea Her Excel Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Her Excel breaks cleanly and faces no genuine pace pressure through the early stages, she dictates a controlled solo lead.
scenarios.body: Sea Her Excel sets a measured tempo that suits her stamina profile, and horses travelling prominently behind — particularly Over Spiced and Queen Sana — are best placed to pick her off if she ties up late. The lack of pressure means the leader preserves energy and the race becomes a stern staying test in the final furlong that suits those who have been travelling sweetly close to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Her Excel's lead is actively pressured by Queen Sana and Over Spiced pushing up aggressively from the outset, the pace collapses in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: A contested pace even at moderate tempo on the AW can stretch the field enough to expose the leader, and a prominent rival who has been tracking comfortably without over-racing delivers the decisive challenge. Over Spiced's consistent placed form at 5f and Queen Sana's runner-up habit put them both in frame to pounce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the prominent horses flatten out inside the final furlong, creating a gap for late challengers.
scenarios.body: Whizzy Dizzy or Independent Expert would need the field to have gone hard enough to create daylight on the stands rail, which is plausible only if early pressure unexpectedly elevates — a lower-probability outcome given Sea Her Excel's uncontested expected lead. La Belle Forest and Little Jaybee are nominally mapped to midfield but are true hold-up types, meaning their chance here is further discounted as they are unlikely to get the run of the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dead Gallop Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Her Excel sets an unusually slow early pace, compressing the field and producing a chaotic sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A messy, bunched finish on a flat 5f AW track gives weight-advantaged and freshest runners an equal chance, making this the most unpredictable shape; Little Jaybee, fresh off an 8-day turnaround, and Fiorella Princess, whose AW Standard form is strong, could benefit from the chaos. However this scenario requires Sea Her Excel to race far below her known front-running style and is assigned minimal probability accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Sea Her Excel's draw and early break are critical — if she misses the kick, the entire race shape unravels and prominent types Queen Sana and Over Spiced inherit the pace scenario with no tested front-runner to beat.
Over Spiced has run exclusively on Good ground in her recent placed sequence; watch for any market drift pre-race that might signal the Standard AW surface is not expected to suit.

La Belle Forest and Little Jaybee are both natural hold-up horses mapped to midfield — monitor how much early traffic they encounter, as a congested inner at Lingfield 5f could cost them vital lengths before the race has even begun.

Fiorella Princess returns from 134 days off; watch paddock behaviour and early market move as Robert Cowell's T14 form (2/9) suggests readiness, but the layoff is the single biggest unknown in the race.

Weight distribution is tight across the field (125-138lbs), but Little Jaybee carries the lightest burden at 125lbs — in a compressed finish her weight allowance could be the marginal factor that Pat Cosgrave looks to exploit.
